prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: what is the net revenue of each parent category from the products that take part in at least one promotion? A product takes part when at least one promotion lists it, and every order line of such a product counts once, whether or not the line was sold with a promotion. Use net_revenue_eur from the sales table. Return two columns, in this order: parent_category and revenue_eur. Return one row for each parent category with such products. Do not round. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check the grain of the bridge table: how many rows does a product in two promotions have?
Each line of such a product meets two bridge rows, so its revenue is added twice; join the lines to a list that holds each product once.
starter_sql:
SELECT s.parent_category, SUM(s.net_revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur
FROM sales s
JOIN promotion_products pp ON pp.product_id = s.product_id
GROUP BY s.parent_category
why_this_works: The step lists each promoted product once, so every line meets one row and its revenue is added once.
